about: Spelling styles: how a word kept as sounds is written in letters. A style changes the default romanisation of sounds.json ('roman', 'alt') only where it says so. See README.md.
sources: The conventions of the Latin-alphabet orthographies the styles are modelled on (Romance, German, West and South Slavic, Scandinavian); Daniels, P. T. & Bright, W. (eds.) 1996. The World's Writing Systems. Oxford University Press.

fields.diacritics: false: every letter is a-z or the apostrophe; an 'alt' with a diacritic is not used, the 'roman' stands
fields.map: sound id → letters; overrides 'roman' and, for a long vowel, longVowel
fields.context: spellings that depend on the neighbours: before/after take V, C, frontV (i e ɛ y æ and their long forms), backV, # (word edge)
fields.longVowel: how a long vowel is written: double (aa), macron (ā), acute (á), circumflex (â), h (ah), single (a: length not shown)
fields.nasalVowel: how a nasal vowel is written: n (an), tilde (ã)
fields.geminate: how two equal consonants are written: double (tt) or single (t)
fields.collision: when two sounds of one inventory get the same letters, the rarer sound (lower weight in sounds.json) takes its 'alt'; if that also collides or is not allowed, the two sounds share the letters (as in many real spellings)
fields.capital: the first letter of a name is a capital; a digraph capitalises only its first letter (Sh, not SH)

styles.note: Modelled on the practical orthographies of Australian and Pacific languages: few letters, digraphs for place.
